# Preparation Functions

Shared executable functions for preparing one configured document attachment, obtaining its document, checking admission and linking prerequisites, and recording readiness. It inherits `prepare`, `create`, `attach` and their validation rules from Attachment Functions. These functions define individual stages; their enclosing workflow determines when those stages run.

## Configuration and inputs

Execution constants identify the attachment and its locations: `key` selects the singleton preparation record at `/preparation_<key>`; `requestPath` holds the prepared specification; `instructionPath` holds the selected document; `statePath` holds the inherited attachment state; and `termsPath` identifies terms checked against the specification. These paths belong to the document executing the functions.

`obtain="create"` selects local creation. Otherwise, `prepared` records `awaiting_document`, but it emits a provision request only for `obtain="provide"`. `actor` identifies the permitted supplier channel. `authority` identifies the role checked for admission, and `admissionKey` selects its amendment clause. Local creation additionally requires `allowCreate`.

For functions using `requireInvocation`, `automatic` selects the authorization check; it does not itself install a trigger. Automatic invocation requires `/activation/active` to be true. Other invocation requires exact-document-version review and, when `/activation` exists, active status, valid participant access and a currently authorized party or representative channel. `provide` additionally requires the channel to equal `actor`.

`prepare` reads clause parameters `template`, `fieldPaths`, `authority` and `hooks`. Its merged defaults are `authority="guarantor"`, `hooks={}`, `payer="customer"` and `payee="seller"`; the shown preparation body does not otherwise use `payer` or `payee`. Other execution-constant defaults are not established here.

`beginPublic` accepts Attachment Preparation Input plus a required `requestId`, then removes the input's `type` before recording its intent. `requestId` must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Optional `values` defaults to an empty object during preparation. Each supplied name must map through `fieldPaths` to a path beginning `/paymentTerms/`, `/destination/` or `/terms/`. `authorityParty` is needed when the configured authority is absent from the current roster; if already present, the supplied profile must have the same primary identity.

## Preparing and obtaining the attachment

`begin` checks invocation authority, validates `requestId`, and calls inherited `prepare`. It then records `requestId`, the complete normalized input as `intent`, `status="preparing"` and an empty `reason`. Repeating the same identifier and intent returns `duplicate`; a different identifier is rejected as a second singleton request, and changed intent under the same identifier is rejected as a conflict.

Inherited `prepare` builds the exact requested document from `template` and permitted `values`. It assigns `instanceKey` from the executing document's identity and `key`, installs the attachment policy, copies participant transports and access-document references, and sets child activation parameters `frozen=true` and `required=[]`. The prepared request records `document`, `documentBlueId`, `policy`, `requirements` and `signals`. An existing request must equal the newly prepared request exactly. Cross-embedded preparation requires an initialized parent document.

`prepared` acts only while the recorded status is `preparing`. It records `creating` for local creation or `awaiting_document` otherwise, clears `reason`, and sets `requiresAdmission` when the relationship is cross-embedded and the authority is absent from the executing document's roster. It emits Document Preparation Requested with `clauseId`, `requestId` and `requirementRef`. In provide mode it also emits Document Provision Requested, addressed to `actor` through `party` and correlated by `inResponseTo`. These events request progress; they do not confirm provision or readiness.

`createPrepared` calls inherited `create` only in create mode, with an existing preparation request and no document at `instructionPath`. Creation checks invocation, `allowCreate`, roster compatibility and any `attachWhen` condition. It installs the prepared child, adding `/sources/parent` and `attachmentLink.parentOrigin` for a cross-embedded relationship. Its attachment state becomes `attached`; this can precede native initialization and activation.

`provide` accepts `document`, `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`. The document must be an initialized publication supplied by Blue ID. Create mode rejects provision. The two references must match the recorded preparation request and its current `documentBlueId`. Successful provision stores the candidate publication reference and its `candidateOrigin`; it does not attach the candidate. Later provision may update the publication of that same origin, but cannot replace it with another origin.

Candidate validation requires an active child, matching prepared source, attachment policy, hooks, terms and `instanceKey`. Source comparison normalizes away activation party declarations and their transport contracts, then checks party identity separately. Primary identity means the same lead channel and identical nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` sets. Every parent role must be represented; only the configured authority may be an additional role.

Inherited `attach` also checks the current parent roster and any `attachWhen.path`/`attachWhen.equals` condition. Cross-embedded attachment requires the authority in the parent, a reverse link to the parent's exact origin, and compatible parties in the candidate's embedded parent view. An existing attachment with another origin is rejected; the same origin returns `duplicate`. Creation and attachment emit configured Source Changed signals, which are distinct from final readiness.

## Admission and readiness

`prepareAdmission` acts only when `requiresAdmission` is true, a candidate exists and no admission proposal is already stored. `admissionKey` must identify exactly an Amendments Clause with nonempty `parameters.approvers`. Its state location comes from that clause's `bindings.state`, defaulting to `/amendments`.

The function stores an amendment proposal using the current amendment revision and a proposal identifier derived from `key` and `requestId`. Its target is `/admission_<key>`. The replacement binds `activationRevision`, `authority`, `candidateOrigin`, the prepared authority `profile`, `requestId` and `requirementRef`. Party Admission Requested reports the proposal identifier and request correlation. Storing and emitting this proposal neither applies the amendment nor admits the party.

`resume` needs no request fields. It returns `duplicate` when no preparation exists or status is already `ready`. Otherwise it records `pending` with `reason="activation"` until the executing document is active. When no document is selected, it needs a candidate and checks these additional waits:

- `amendment`: the stored admission proposal is missing or `/admission_<key>` does not exactly equal its replacement.
- `party_admission`: the cross-embedded authority is still absent from the parent roster.
- `reverse_link`: the cross-embedded candidate has no `attachmentLink.parentOrigin`.

After these checks, `resume` revalidates the candidate and invokes inherited `attach`, which also checks the reverse link's exact value. An absent candidate produces a no-op, not a readiness confirmation.

`settle` requires a selected document. It records `pending`/`activation` while the executing document is inactive, `selected`/`native_initialization` while the child lacks `contracts.initialized.document`, and `selected`/`child_activation` while the child is inactive. Once these checks pass, it records `ready`, clears `reason`, stores `documentOrigin`, and emits Document Attached with `documentPath`, `documentOrigin`, `relationship`, `clauseId` and `inResponseTo`. `documentOrigin` identifies the child's initial document, whereas the candidate reference identifies a supplied publication.

`ready` records readiness observed at settlement. Both `resume` and `settle` stop rechecking once it is recorded, so it does not guarantee continuing activation. Missing lifecycle fields are unknown.

`progress` merges supplied fields into the preparation record and emits Document Attachment Pending with `status`, `reason` and request correlation. It returns `duplicate` when status and reason compare unchanged, even if other input fields differ; missing reasons count as empty for this comparison and event emission. It does not restrict status to a fixed enum. The statuses above are those written by the supplied stage functions.

An `acceptedNew` result means that stage accepted its work, not that attachment is ready. A `duplicate` result can also mean a guard caused no work; it is not a completion certificate.

## Hook relationships

`allowed` limits hook action names. Hooks default to `in="instruction"` and `on="workflow"`. Instruction-local hooks must use workflow mode. Parent hooks must use state or event mode and make the relationship `cross-embedded`; without parent hooks it is `one-way`. `kind="document"` omits the generated hooks clause; other kinds use `requestType`. `instructionType` is recorded in the prepared requirements.

Parent state hooks require `path` and `equals`; parent event hooks require `event`. Parent hooks check that the parent selected this child, remains active, includes the authority, and retains matching primary parties. Optional `recheckOn` is allowed only for parent state hooks, forbids supplied `before`/`after` effects, requires document-only `params` and `when` expressions, and accepts distinct non-root paths outside `/sources`. These checks constrain hook execution; they do not establish that its business action has completed.
